title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction in General K-Algebras
description: Formalizes modular reduction via the minimal polynomial in general K-algebras: evaluating f at x equals evaluating f mod minpoly(x). Also proves base change behavior in algebra towers K ⊂ L ⊂ A, showing degree can only decrease when extending the base field.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)

mathlibDependencies.description: Minimal polynomial of an integral element is monic
Minimal polynomial is irreducible over the base field
Division algorithm: f = (f mod m) + m * (f div m)
Degree of divisor bounded by degree of dividend

originalContributions: minpoly_reduction: aeval x f = aeval x (f mod minpoly) for any integral x in a K-algebra
minpoly_annihilator_iff: aeval x f = 0 ↔ minpoly K x | f (full characterization)
minpoly_congruence_iff: aeval x f = aeval x g ↔ minpoly K x | (f - g)
power_reduction: x^k = aeval x (X^k mod minpoly) for higher power computation
minpoly_dvd_map_of_tower: minpoly L x | (minpoly K x).map(algebraMap K L) in towers
minpoly_natDegree_tower_le: degree over L ≤ degree over K
minpoly_eq_map_of_irreducible: equality when base-changed minpoly stays irreducible (1 sorry)

overview.historicalContext:
**Minimal Polynomial Arithmetic in Algebras**

The minimal polynomial of an algebraic element x in a K-algebra A generates the kernel of the evaluation map K[X] → A. This means polynomial arithmetic modulo the minimal polynomial captures all algebraic relations satisfied by x. When working in a tower K ⊂ L ⊂ A, the minimal polynomial over L divides the base change of the one over K, so the degree can only decrease with larger base fields.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize (1) modular reduction of polynomial evaluation via the minimal polynomial in general K-algebras, and (2) base change behavior of minimal polynomials in algebra towers.
overview.proofStrategy: For modular reduction: use the division algorithm f = (f mod m) + m · q, then evaluate at x where m(x) = 0. For tower divisibility: map minpoly K x through algebraMap K L to get an annihilating polynomial over L, then apply the universal property of the minimal polynomial over L.
keyInsights: Evaluating f(x) only depends on f mod minpoly(x) — higher-degree information is annihilated
The annihilator ideal of x is exactly the principal ideal generated by the minimal polynomial
In algebra towers, the minimal polynomial degree can only decrease when extending the base field
Equality in towers holds precisely when the base-changed polynomial remains irreducible

sections.title: Core Reduction Theorem
sections.summary: The fundamental theorem: aeval x f = aeval x (f mod minpoly K x), with corollaries for the quotient and difference.

sections.title: Annihilator Characterization
sections.summary: Full characterization: aeval x f = 0 ↔ minpoly K x | f. The annihilator ideal is closed under addition and multiplication.

sections.title: Congruence and Quotient Structure
sections.summary: Congruence: aeval x f = aeval x g ↔ minpoly K x | (f - g). Same remainder implies same evaluation.

sections.title: Degree Bounds
sections.summary: The remainder has degree strictly less than the minimal polynomial, which has positive degree in domains.

sections.title: Power Reduction
sections.summary: Powers x^k reduce via the minimal polynomial. The element x itself reduces to X mod minpoly.

sections.title: Special Elements
sections.summary: Minimal polynomial divisibility for idempotent (x²=x), involutory (x²=1), and nilpotent (x^d=0) elements.

sections.title: Algebra Tower Reduction
sections.summary: Base change: minpoly L x | (minpoly K x).map(algebraMap K L). Degree bound and equality condition (1 sorry).

conclusion.summary: This file develops two complementary theories: (1) modular arithmetic of polynomial evaluation via the minimal polynomial, showing that evaluation depends only on the remainder mod minpoly, and (2) base change behavior in algebra towers, proving degree can only decrease. All results except the irreducibility equality condition are fully verified.
conclusion.implications: The modular reduction theory provides the algebraic foundation for efficient computation in quotient algebras K[x]/(minpoly). The tower results extend the K-algebra invariance theory to base-ring-changing transformations.
openQuestions: Complete the sorry in minpoly_eq_map_of_irreducible (show associated monic polynomials are equal)
Can the minpoly over L be characterized via irreducible factors of the mapped minpoly?
